en.title: 10 Must-Watch Movies Dropping on Streaming This October
en.summary: As the leaves turn and the nights grow longer, October's streaming slate is packed with must-see films, from bone-chilling horror to acclaimed dramas, perfect for your cozy nights in.
en.body:
## 1. Evil Dead Burn
Get ready for a gruesome good time as the ninth installment of the iconic horror franchise unleashes its full, grotesque power. "Evil Dead Burn" promises to be an ultra-violent, effects-laden ride that fans of the series have been craving, hitting HBO Max on October 2nd.

## 2. The Invite
Olivia Wilde directs and stars in this darkly comedic relationship drama that's already being hailed as one of the year's best films. It delves into the awkward dynamics of a dinner party gone awry, featuring a star-studded cast including Seth Rogen and Edward Norton, and lands on HBO Max October 23rd.

## 3. War
Kicking off the month on HBO Max is "War," a gripping cinematic experience that is sure to set an intense tone for October. Premiering on October 1st, this film is poised to be a significant release for those seeking powerful storytelling.

## 4. The Death of Robin Hood
Prepare for a fresh take on a legendary tale as "The Death of Robin Hood" makes its debut on HBO Max on October 16th. This A24 production hints at a more mature and perhaps darker interpretation of the beloved outlaw story.

## 5. Disclosure Day
While specific streaming details are still emerging, "Disclosure Day" is generating buzz as a significant new film hitting platforms this October. Its inclusion on critical lists suggests a compelling narrative that fans of topical cinema won't want to miss.

## 6. The French Dispatch
Wes Anderson's visually distinct and star-studded ode to journalism arrives on streaming, offering a delightful ensemble cast and his signature quirky storytelling. Its unique blend of humor and heartfelt moments makes it a standout choice for cinephiles seeking artistic flair.

## 7. Dune: Part Two
Experience the breathtaking continuation of Denis Villeneuve's sci-fi epic as "Dune: Part Two" becomes available for home viewing. The visually stunning and narratively rich conclusion to Paul Atreides' journey is a must-see for its grand scale and immersive world-building.

## 8. The Zone of Interest
This Palme d'Or winner offers a chilling and unique perspective on the banality of evil, focusing on the domestic life of Rudolf Höss and his family living next to Auschwitz. Its thought-provoking and unsettling nature makes it a profound cinematic achievement.

## 9. Poor Things
Emma Stone delivers a tour-de-force performance in Yorgos Lanthimos's surreal and darkly comedic tale of a young woman brought back to life by an eccentric scientist. Its bold visual style and unconventional narrative promise a truly unforgettable viewing experience.

## 10. Anatomy of a Fall
Winner of the Palme d'Or, this gripping French courtroom drama dissects a marriage and a potential murder with razor-sharp precision. The film's intricate plotting and compelling performances make it a masterclass in suspense and character study.
Bottom Line: This October, the streaming landscape is dominated by horror thrills and critically acclaimed dramas that promise to captivate and provoke.
